generator: Written by IterFixtureGen (Legacy/IterKit) with the old IterData module.
expected.json: a copy of the fixture opened with IterSchema.makeContainer(url:) + IterStore(container:) (migrates to V4, runs flattenFolders), then read back.
as-written.json: the fixture read back before any migration (V1-V3 with the frozen schema and no migration plan; V4 with the live code).
Dates are timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate Doubles; UUIDs are uppercase; arrays are sorted by id except stopIDs of a trip (orderedStops order).
flattenFolders sets updatedAt to the time of generation on every flattened folder (listed in flattenedFolderIDs); those values change on regeneration.

places.name: Hamnøy bridge ✨
places.notes: 北極光 chance in Sept–Mar. Wind!

places.blurb: A granite-rimmed reservoir under the Sierra crest, ringed by aspens that turn gold and orange in October.
places.name: Lake Sabrina
places.notes: 30 min up CA-168 from Bishop. Fall colour usually peaks late Sept–mid Oct (check the Eastern Sierra fall colour report). Calm dawn water for reflections; the road can close with early snow.

places.blurb: Folded mudstone badlands ripple toward Manly Beacon while the Panamints blush on the horizon. Pure sunrise theatre.
places.name: Zabriskie Point
places.notes: Paved 5 min uphill walk from the lot. Busy at dawn year-round; arrive 40 min early. Telephoto (70–200mm) picks out the light on the ridgelines. Avoid midday May–Sept — 45°C+.

places.blurb: Limestone towers standing in a salt lake twice as old as the Sierra, glassy and pink before the wind wakes up.
places.name: South Tufa, Mono Lake
places.notes: $3 day-use fee, 1 mi loop boardwalk. Do not climb or touch tufa. Mornings are usually calm for reflections; bring bug spray in June for alkali flies. Milky Way rises over the lake to the southeast.

places.blurb: A dry waterfall of polished black basalt, carved by a river that vanished 10,000 years ago. Empty after dark.
places.name: Fossil Falls
places.notes: Signed turn off US-395, then 0.5 mi walk on rough lava. No rails at the drop — scout the edges in daylight. Great paired with Alabama Hills on the same night.

places.blurb: A natural arch framing Mount Whitney, with some of the darkest accessible skies in California.
places.name: Mobius Arch, Alabama Hills
places.notes: Short loop from Movie Road. Frame Whitney through the arch at dawn alpenglow; Milky Way core rises to the south in spring/summer. Free BLM camping nearby.

places.blurb: A gold-rush town left exactly where it fell — pews, pool tables and 1940s trucks bleaching in high-desert light.
places.name: Bodie Ghost Town
places.notes: Last 3 mi are washboard gravel; road closes with snow. Park hours roughly 9am–6pm (shorter in winter), so golden hour means late-summer evenings. Shoot through the windows; night access only on ranger-led photo events.

places.blurb: Hexagonal salt polygons to the horizon, 86 m below sea level, with Telescope Peak glowing pink above them at dawn.
places.name: Badwater Basin
places.notes: Boardwalk from the lot; the crisp polygons start about 1.5 mi out on the flat. After rare winter rain, shallow water gives reflections of the Panamints. Wide lens low to the ground.

places.blurb: The Colorado River wraps a perfect 270° curve 300 m below the rim. The canyon is best just after sunrise, before the shadow and the tour buses arrive.
places.name: Horseshoe Bend
places.notes: $10 parking fee; 1.5 mi round trip on a graded path. You need 14mm or wider (or a vertical pano) to fit the whole bend. Sunset brings a starburst but deep shadow in the bend. Arizona does not observe DST.

places.name: Mobius Arch pullout
places.notes: Dark sky, Bortle 2. Flat gravel, room for the star tracker.

places.blurb: A freestanding 16 m arch on the lip of a slickrock bowl, burning red against the snow-capped La Sals at sunset.
places.name: Delicate Arch — golden hour 🌅
places.notes:
Hike starts at the Wolfe Ranch lot.
Bring a headlamp for the walk down.

places.blurb: Twisted pines more than 4,000 years old under a sky black enough to see the Milky Way cast shadows.
places.name: Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest
places.notes: Schulman Grove is about 1 hr from Bishop; road usually open May–Nov. At 3,000 m nights are cold — pack layers. Low-level light painting on the trunks, never bright lights.

places.blurb: Mount Morrison’s striped face catches first light and drops it straight into the lake. Aspens go gold here in early October.
places.name: Convict Lake
places.notes: 5 min off US-395, paved lot at the shore. The 2.5 mi flat loop gives compositions from every side. Calm water is most likely in the first hour after sunrise.

places.blurb: Knife-edge ridges and wind ripples lit from the side — the only hour of the day the dunes have texture.
places.name: Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes
places.notes: Park at the Stovepipe Wells lot; walk 20–30 min out to escape footprints. Sidelight within 45 min of sunrise/sunset. Carry water and a headlamp; dunes are easy to get turned around in after dark.
